report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Builds a derived text brief of a file graph: symbols, imports (including function-body edges), and document claims, with an honest truncation report.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BUDGET_CHARS
symbols.note: Default character budget for a whole brief; 12,000 chars.

symbols.name: DEEP_EDGE_MARK
symbols.note: Marks an edge that exists only inside a function body; '*'.

symbols.name: ARTEFACT_ROOTS
symbols.note: Path prefixes that are artefacts, never project; ('runs/', 'build/', 'dist/', '.captures/').

symbols.name: _is_artefact
symbols.note: Returns True if rel starts with any ARTEFACT_ROOTS.

symbols.name: GraphBrief
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding rendered brief text, targets, neighbours, counts, dropped, provenance.

symbols.name: char_count
symbols.note: Property; length of the brief text.

symbols.name: truncated
symbols.note: Property; True if any layer dropped items.

symbols.name: _sig
symbols.note: Builds a signature string from an ast.FunctionDef or ast.AsyncFunctionDef, including posonly, args, vararg, kwonlyargs, kwarg, and async prefix.

symbols.name: file_symbols
symbols.note: Returns top-level API of one Python file as declaration lines; includes class methods one level down; skips dunder methods except __init__; includes module-level UPPER_CASE assignments as 'NAME = ...'.

symbols.name: _deep_only_modules
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of dotted module names imported only inside function bodies (deep minus top-level).

symbols.name: _tail_matches
symbols.note: Suffix-matches dotted names against a relative path; handles .py suffix, __init__ stripping, and two-level tails.

symbols.name: _neighbourhood
symbols.note: BFS over edges and reverse edges up to hops, excluding artefact paths, returning sorted neighbours not in targets.

symbols.name: graph_brief
symbols.note: Builds the brief for targets and their neighbourhood; uses cached index if index is None; never raises for missing index.

claims.text: the agents never see the graph. No provider module references ``structcore``, ``build_index``, ``typegraph`` or ``forest``.
claims.why: This chunk does not enumerate provider modules; the claim is about the whole codebase.

claims.text: All three of those hallucinations are answered by ~6.5k characters of text that the index can already produce.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the index output or its size; the 6,479 figure is cited elsewhere in the comment block but not verifiable here.

claims.text: Function-body edges are marked ``*``: 202 of 526 internal edges in this repo are only visible there, so a brief built from top-level imports alone would present ~60% of the graph as the whole of it.
claims.why: The numbers 202/526 are not derivable from this chunk; they refer to repo-wide measurements.

claims.text: Layers 2 and 3 degrade cleanly: the type and document layers of the index are behind flags, and when they are off those sections are omitted rather than faked.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the layer-rendering code; only the module docstring states this.

claims.text: What is never omitted silently is a TRUNCATION -- if the budget cuts the brief, the brief says what it dropped.
claims.why: The rendering code that reports dropped items is in the next chunk; this chunk only defines the GraphBrief.dropped field and truncated property.

claims.text: This is a DERIVED artefact. It is regenerated, never edited
claims.why: The module does not enforce regeneration; it is a policy statement about the repo.

claims.text: a model must not cite it as evidence about behaviour -- it describes shape, not semantics.
claims.why: This is a usage instruction; not checkable against code.

claims.text: the full symbol layer for the ``daedalus/`` package is 6,479 characters
claims.why: The measurement is not in this chunk; it is a comment claim.

claims.text: the first brief built for ``daedalus/shift.py`` listed ``runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py`` as a graph neighbour and printed its symbols. That file is the DESTROYED artefact kept as evidence
claims.why: The historical incident is not verifiable from this chunk; the artefact root tuple is present but the incident is a comment.

claims.text: ``build/`` -- holds 142 stale copies of the package
claims.why: The count is a comment claim; not in code.

claims.text: a brief that lists a symbol twice from two versions of one file is worse than one that omits it
claims.why: This is a design rationale; not a code behaviour.

claims.text: overshooting the reserve wastes a few hundred characters, while under-reserving silently pushes the brief over the budget a caller sized its prompt against.
claims.why: The reserve is 700; the rendering logic that uses it is in the next chunk.

claims.text: Signatures rather than bare names, because the measured failure was not only "the module does not exist" but "the module does not define that": a name without its shape still lets a caller invent the arguments.
claims.why: file_symbols returns _sig(node) which includes parameter names and async prefix, not just bare names.

claims.text: Methods are included one level down for classes, since ``Shift.tick()`` is the kind of thing a caller needs and the class name alone does not give it.
claims.why: The ClassDef branch iterates node.body and appends '    ' + _sig(sub) for FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef.

claims.text: Deeper nesting is deliberately not listed -- it is not API.
claims.why: The function only walks tree.body and one level into ClassDef.body; no deeper recursion.

claims.text: the index publishes a flat edge list with no depth: it correctly INCLUDES function-body edges (12 edges for ``offload.py`` against 7 top-level import statements -- verified), it just cannot say which ones they are.
claims.why: The 12/7 numbers are not in this chunk; the index is external.

claims.text: One extra AST pass over a handful of neighbour files buys the distinction.
claims.why: _deep_only_modules does an AST parse and walk to compute deep-only modules.

claims.text: Over-matching here only ever adds a ``*`` mark to an edge that is genuinely present, so a wrong guess mislabels a true edge rather than inventing one.
claims.why: _tail_matches returns True on suffix match; a false positive would mark an existing edge with '*', which is a mislabelling, not an invented edge.

claims.text: ``index`` may be supplied to avoid a rebuild; otherwise the process-wide cached index is used, which is single-flight, so two hundred concurrent lanes warm it once rather than each starting a full scan.
claims.why: The cached_index import and its single-flight property are in the next chunk; this chunk only shows the import attempt.

claims.text: Never raises for a missing or unreadable index: a lane that cannot get a brief must still be able to run with none.
claims.why: The error handling around cached_index is in the next chunk; this chunk ends at the import statement.

observations.what: _deep_only_modules uses ast.walk which descends into nested functions and classes, so it captures imports inside any nested scope, not just top-level function bodies.
file_symbols treats any module-level ast.Assign with an UPPER_CASE target as a constant, but does not handle ast.AnnAssign or ast.AugAssign; such declarations will be omitted.
_sig omits default values and type annotations; the docstring says 'signatures' but the output is parameter names only.
GraphBrief.truncated returns True if any dropped value is truthy; if a layer drops zero items it is falsy, but if a count is negative (impossible by construction) it would also be truthy.
_neighbourhood uses set of targets; if targets contains duplicates, they are deduplicated, which is fine.

risks: _deep_only_modules | low | ast.walk descends into all nested scopes, so imports inside class bodies or nested functions are also classified as 'deep', which may over-mark edges as function-body-only when they are inside a class method. | Check whether the intended 'function body' includes class methods; if so, the current behaviour is correct.
